intro: La Lande-Patry is a village on the western edge of Flers, in the bocage country of the Orne in Normandy. On the Rue de l'Église stands a yew whose trunk has gone hollow, splitting into a ring of thick fluted columns with a tall dark doorway into its heart. A reader sent us its photograph and puts it at about a thousand years old. No register we hold lists it yet, so the page says what is known.

trees.story:
A reader sent this yew from the Rue de l'Église in La Lande-Patry, a village next to Flers in the Orne, Normandy, and gave it an age of about a thousand years.

The photograph is taken close in, and it is all trunk. The yew is hollow. Its base has split into a ring of thick, fluted columns of red-brown and grey wood, and between two of them a tall opening runs from the ground to above head height, a dark doorway into the empty heart, its floor covered in bark chips. Twisting limbs spread above. Thin metal stakes stand at the foot of the trunk, a stone slab lies in front of it, and a stone monument stands on the grass behind.

Old yews commonly go hollow and keep growing, so the opening is no sign the tree is failing. The age is the reader's estimate, and we have no girth, ring count or register entry for this tree, so read it as theirs. If you have measured it or know its history, tell us here.

Look for the dark doorway in the trunk.
